candidates.attacker_control: The YAML document body is fully attacker-controlled whenever the parser handles untrusted input: (a) SwaggerParser.parse(String)/readWithInfo(String) pass the caller-supplied string directly to DeserializationUtils.readYamlTree; (b) SwaggerParser.read(location)/Swagger20Parser.readWithInfo(location) download or read a spec from a URL/file/classpath location and parse its body the same way; (c) external $ref contents fetched by ResolverCache.loadRef are parsed through DeserializationUtils.deserialize/deserializeIntoTree, which call readYamlTree for non-JSON content. An attacker who can submit, host, or influence the referenced specification controls the YAML text and therefore its tags.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The JSON branch (Json.mapper().readTree) has no polymorphic typing enabled and is not affected; the Jackson YAML mapper path (Yaml.mapper().readValue in DeserializationUtils.deserialize) is safe. The repository poms do not declare SnakeYAML directly (it is transitive via swagger-core/jackson-dataformat-yaml), so the exact version cannot be confirmed from this snapshot; only SnakeYAML 1.x semantics make the no-arg Yaml() unsafe. The poms do contain a snakeyaml exclusion, but only for TestNG, not for the runtime path. No SafeConstructor, tag filter, or LoaderOptions appears anywhere in the snapshot (verified by search). No runtime execution was performed and this is not claimed to be runtime-confirmed.
candidates.impact: Remote code execution in the JVM that parses the specification (class loading and gadget/static-initializer execution under the parser's privileges), or at minimum arbitrary object instantiation and denial of service. Confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact on the host application rather than a mere parsing error.
candidates.prerequisites: Application code passes untrusted specification content (string, file, or URL) to swagger-parser, and a SnakeYAML version whose default Yaml() constructor still performs unsafe global-tag object construction is on the classpath. This project does not pin SnakeYAML in its own poms; it arrives transitively via io.swagger:swagger-core 1.5.15 -> jackson-dataformat-yaml -> org.yaml:snakeyaml, i.e. a 1.x-era SnakeYAML where the no-arg constructor is unsafe. Standard JDK classes (javax.script.ScriptEngineManager, java.net.URLClassLoader) are sufficient for the documented SnakeYAML RCE pattern.
candidates.root_cause: DeserializationUtils.readYamlTree()/readYamlValue() instantiate org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml with its default constructor and call yaml.load(contents) on untrusted spec text (lines 59-67). The default SnakeYAML constructor is the unsafe Constructor, which resolves global tags (e.g. !!javax.script.ScriptEngineManager combined with !!java.net.URLClassLoader) and instantiates the named Java classes during parsing. No SafeConstructor, tag filtering, alias limit, or loader options are applied. This is the YAML branch of the parser: any input that does not start with '{' is routed here.
candidates.title: Unsafe SnakeYAML deserialization of attacker-supplied YAML in DeserializationUtils (CWE-502)
candidates.trace: SwaggerParser.parse(String) / readWithInfo(String) -> input not starting with '{' -> DeserializationUtils.readYamlTree(contents) lines 59-62 -> new org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml() + yaml.load(contents) -> SnakeYAML instantiates classes named by !! global tags. Same sink from Swagger20Parser.convertToSwagger/readWithInfo (lines 60-65, 117-122) for specs fetched from URL/file/classpath, and from ResolverCache.loadRef -> DeserializationUtils.deserialize/deserializeIntoTree (lines 121, 127) for external $ref contents.
candidates.unverified: Exact transitive SnakeYAML version on the deployed classpath; whether consuming applications actually parse attacker-influenced YAML rather than only trusted specs; whether a specific gadget chain is required in the target environment. No exploitation was attempted.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data (unsafe SnakeYAML object construction)

coverage_summary: All 141 source-root files were listed. Both modules' Java sources were read or searched: swagger-parser (SwaggerParser, Swagger20Parser, SwaggerResolver, ResolverCache, all processors, RefUtils, RemoteUrl, DeserializationUtils, PathUtils, ClasspathHelper, HostAuthorizationValue, SwaggerDeserializer sampled/searched) and swagger-compat-spec-parser (SwaggerCompatConverter, SwaggerLegacyParser, readers, deserializers, HttpClient, validator/transform/migrate utilities, MutableJsonTree). Both module poms, the root pom, README, and build configs were inspected. Large resources (patches/t.json, 300 KB sample specs, JSON schemas) were only searched, not read end-to-end; they are data/schema files. No code execution, build, dependency resolution, or external lookups were performed.
limitations: No test sources are present in the snapshot, so no test names or fixtures could corroborate the intended vulnerability.

The exact transitive SnakeYAML version is not pinned in this repository (it comes via io.swagger:swagger-core 1.5.15), so unsafe-constructor behavior is inferred from the unversioned no-arg Yaml() usage and the 1.x-era dependency set rather than confirmed from a lock file.
swagger-models (io.swagger.models.refs.RefFormat and RefProperty/RefModel constructors) is an external dependency not included in this snapshot, limiting certainty on the SSRF/path-traversal lead.
The 1657-line SwaggerDeserializer.java and all resource/schema/sample JSON files were not read line-by-line; some low-level parsing edge cases may remain uninspected.
No source build, static-analysis run, or runtime reproduction was performed; all statements are static source observations.

rejected_leads.lead: SSRF / local file read reachable through parser location and $ref resolution (Swagger20Parser, RemoteUrl, RefUtils, SwaggerCompatConverter)
rejected_leads.reason: Real design weakness (no scheme allow-list, no path containment check in parentDirectory.resolve(file).normalize(), compat converter concatenates ref paths onto the parent directory), but this is largely the documented purpose of a parser that reads specs from a location and resolves external refs; $ref scheme classification happens in the external swagger-models RefFormat code, which is not in this snapshot, so exact routing could not be confirmed statically. Kept as an unconfirmed lead rather than a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: RemoteUrl trust-all TLS (X509TrustManager and HostnameVerifier returning true) in createConnectionConfigurator
rejected_leads.reason: Fully gated behind the opt-in JVM system property RemoteUrl(...).trustAll / README TRUST_ALL; disabled by default, so it is a documented dangerous option, not an active vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Potential DoS / index bug in RefUtils.buildUrl for relative $refs with more than one leading '..' segment
rejected_leads.reason: At most an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException wrapped as a RuntimeException while loading a malformed ref; no data or memory exposure evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: Header/query injection via AuthorizationValue in RemoteUrl
rejected_leads.reason: Authorization values are supplied by the embedding application, not by parsed spec content; no attacker-controlled path from parsed input to these fields was found.
Contains an explicit destination containment check (dstFile.startsWith(RESOURCE_PATH)) and is a developer utility, not a library entry point.

rejected_leads.lead: Jackson polymorphic deserialization in the compat module
rejected_leads.reason: @JsonTypeInfo uses Id.NAME with an explicit closed @JsonSubTypes list and plain ObjectMapper instances; no default typing or class-name-driven construction exists.

summary: The snapshot is swagger-api/swagger-parser 1.0.30 (modules swagger-parser and swagger-compat-spec-parser); no test sources are present. I traced the reader/resolver entry points, remote-URL fetching, $ref resolution, the compat converter, YAML/JSON deserialization helpers, schema/patch utilities, and the poms. The single strongest source-evidenced candidate is unsafe SnakeYAML deserialization in io.swagger.parser.util.DeserializationUtils: attacker-supplied YAML is loaded with the no-argument org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml() constructor (unsafe SnakeYAML Constructor), which allows arbitrary Java type instantiation from global YAML tags and therefore code execution in the parsing JVM. It is reachable from the normal parsing surface (SwaggerParser.parse(String), SwaggerParser.read/readWithInfo for URL, file and classpath locations, and from external $ref contents resolved via ResolverCache). Other suspicious areas (SSRF / local file read via location or $ref in Swagger20Parser/RemoteUrl/RefUtils/SwaggerCompatConverter) are real design weaknesses but read as caller-controlled location resolution rather than a library-introduced flaw; they are reported only as an unconfirmed lead, not as an additional candidate.
